The later action only inspects or edits the artifact without running it.
The execution invokes a different path or a copy not traceable to the creation action.

name: LAUNCHES_DETACHED_LONG_RUNNING_SERVICE
definition: The action starts a long-running server process detached from the invoking shell, with its output redirected, so the process keeps running after the call returns.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The invocation that starts the service in the background.

assertion_conditions: The command detaches the process from the calling shell and redirects its output to a log or equivalent sink.
The invocation reports a process identifier or otherwise acknowledges the detached start.
exclusion_conditions: The server is started in the foreground and blocks the invocation.
The command runs a short-lived operation expected to finish within the call.
The process is started without detachment or output redirection.

name: PROBES_DEPLOYED_SERVICE_ENDPOINT
definition: The action sends one or more crafted requests to the HTTP endpoint of an already running service, and the resulting observation records the returned status codes and response bodies for those requests.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The action issuing the requests to the live endpoint.

parameters.name: observation
parameters.description: The tool result recording the returned statuses and payloads.

assertion_conditions: The requests target the deployed service over the network rather than importing its code in-process.
The payloads are constructed to exercise the endpoint, including valid inputs and/or invalid-input cases intended to produce error statuses.
The observation reports the returned status code and body for at least one issued request.
exclusion_conditions: The action only starts or inspects the process without sending requests.
The invocation fails before any request reaches the service, so no response is recorded.
The action targets a different endpoint or a service that is not running.

name: VERIFIES_REACHABILITY_VIA_EXTERNAL_INTERFACE
definition: The action addresses the deployed service through a non-loopback network address, and the observation's successful response confirms that the service is bound to all interfaces rather than localhost only.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The action contacting the service through the non-loopback address.

parameters.name: observation
parameters.description: The tool result reporting the response obtained over that address.

assertion_conditions: The request URL or host used by the action is a non-loopback address of the service host.
The observation reports a successful response from that address, establishing external reachability.
exclusion_conditions: The request is sent only to the loopback address, which cannot distinguish all-interfaces binding from localhost-only binding.
The attempt over the non-loopback address fails or returns no response.
The service is not running or the address does not belong to the service host.

name: ALLOCATES_EXTENDED_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT
definition: The action explicitly assigns an extended execution time budget to an invocation anticipated to take nontrivial time, such as a remote artifact download, a first-time model load, a service warm-up, or a network probe.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The invocation carrying the extended time budget.

assertion_conditions: The invocation's arguments include an explicit timeout or time-budget setting.
The invoked command involves work that can reasonably take nontrivial time, such as bulk downloading, model loading, sleeping for warm-up, or network requests.
exclusion_conditions: No explicit timeout is set and the invocation relies on the environment default.
The timeout is set for a command expected to complete instantly with no anticipated delay.
The timeout value is present but the command does not involve the long-running work it is meant to accommodate.

name: ATTRIBUTES_FAILURE_TO_OWN_TEST_HARNESS
definition: The reasoning diagnoses an observed negative result as originating in the agent's own verification code or test-input construction rather than in the artifact or service under test, thereby locating the fault in the check rather than in the target system.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text diagnosing the cause of the negative result.

parameters.name: failure
parameters.description: The prior observation whose reported unsuccessful result is being diagnosed.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning explicitly identifies the cause of the failure as a defect in the agent's own test code, script, or input construction (for example, a value of the wrong type or encoding being supplied to the test client).
The reasoning distinguishes that defect from a fault in the system or artifact being tested.
The failure reported by the observation is the one the reasoning addresses.
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning attributes the failure to the target system's implementation, configuration, or environment.
The reasoning merely reports or restates the failure without assigning a cause.
The reasoning proposes correcting the target system rather than the test procedure.

name: REEXECUTES_CHECK_WITH_CORRECTED_TEST_INPUT
definition: After the reasoning diagnoses a concrete defect in how a previous test input or request was constructed, the action repeats the same check against the same target behavior with that input defect corrected, leaving the system under test unchanged.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The repeated invocation that exercises the same behavior using the corrected test input.

parameters.name: diagnosis
parameters.description: The reasoning that names the specific defect in the earlier test input and states the correction.

assertion_conditions: The diagnosis identifies a concrete defect in how the previous test request or input was formed, such as a type, encoding, or formatting mismatch.
The action exercises the same target behavior, endpoint, or property as the earlier attempt, with the identified input defect corrected.
The action leaves the system under test unmodified and changes only the test input.
exclusion_conditions: The action changes the behavior under test, the endpoint, or the scope of the check.
The action repairs, reconfigures, or restarts the target system.
No preceding diagnosis of a test-input defect is present.
The corrected aspect is the form of a tool invocation that the tool itself rejected; correcting an invocation form is a distinct mechanism.

name: ADAPTS_VERIFICATION_TO_ALTERNATIVE_TOOLING
definition: An observation reports that a tool or command needed for a planned check is unavailable, the reasoning chooses a substitute mechanism that obtains the same verification property, and the subsequent action implements that substitute instead of the unavailable tool.

parameters.name: unavailability
parameters.description: The observation reporting that the intended tool, command, or utility is missing or unusable for availability reasons.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text selecting a substitute mechanism that preserves the verification goal.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The invocation that performs the check through the substitute mechanism.

assertion_conditions: The observation establishes unavailability of a specific tool or command, rather than a negative result about the property being verified.
The reasoning explicitly substitutes a different mechanism that targets the same verification property, and states the substitute.
The action implements the substitute mechanism rather than the unavailable one, and follows the reasoning.
exclusion_conditions: The unavailable tool is installed or restored and then used as originally planned.
The substitute check targets a different property than the original verification intent.
The reported failure is a genuine result about the system under test rather than a missing tool.
The earlier observation was merely inconclusive in output while the same tool remained available; re-verification through another access path is a distinct mechanism.

name: INDEPENDENTLY_CORROBORATES_PRIOR_RESULT
definition: A later observation drawn from a different evidence channel than an earlier result, such as runtime logs, process state, or request history, contains concrete entries or identifiers that match the outcome reported earlier, so that outcome is corroborated independently of the original probe.

parameters.name: corroborating
parameters.description: The later observation from an independent evidence source such as service logs or process metadata.

parameters.name: prior_result
parameters.description: The earlier observation whose reported outcome is being corroborated.

assertion_conditions: The corroborating observation derives from a different evidence source than the prior result, not from repeating the same probe.
The corroborating observation contains concrete entries, values, addresses, or identifiers that correspond to the outcome reported by the prior result.
The corroborating observation follows the prior result.
exclusion_conditions: The two observations are merely topically similar or temporally adjacent without matching concrete values.
The corroborating observation contradicts rather than matches the earlier result.
The later observation is a re-run of the same check against the same source with no independent channel.

name: ASSERTS_REQUIREMENTS_VERIFIED
definition: The reasoning audits the task requirement by requirement, associating each stated requirement or deliverable with a concrete observed outcome, and concludes that all of them are satisfied and the task is complete.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text giving the requirement-by-requirement completion assessment.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning enumerates multiple distinct requirements or deliverables of the task rather than a single overall claim.
Each enumerated item is tied to a concrete observed result rather than to an assumption, plan, or intention.
The reasoning explicitly concludes that all enumerated requirements are met or that the task is complete.
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning describes planned or remaining future actions instead of completed verification.
At least one enumerated requirement is left unverified or acknowledged as unresolved.
The reasoning reports individual results without mapping them onto the task's requirements or without an overall completion conclusion.

name: REPORTS_UNAVAILABLE_ENVIRONMENT_TOOL_ALT_PLACEHOLDER
definition: Placeholder removed; not used.

parameters.name: observation
parameters.description: Unused.

assertion_conditions: Unused.
exclusion_conditions: Unused.
